newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian expert forecasts massive AIDS epidemic.
newsitem.headline: Russian expert forecasts massive AIDS epidemic.

text.p: Half a million Russians could be infected over the next two years with the HIV virus that leads to AIDS, Interfax news agency quoted the head of an agency set up to combat the disease as saying on Wednesday.
The forecast made by Professor Vadim Pokrovsky represents an explosive epidemic in a country where registered cases of HIV number little more than 2,000 -- twice as many as a year ago.
Povkrovsky, who called on parliament to approve urgently an anti-AIDS programme, estimated that today's actual number of HIV sufferers, including those not registered, was around 10,000.

The professor, who heads the Russian Scientific Systematic Centre for Prevention and the Fight Against AIDS, was quoted forecasting that by the end of next year 100,000 people could be infected with HIV and 500,000 a year later.
Pokrovsky, whose statement came a day after a coordinator of Russia's anti-AIDS programme rang similar alarm bells, noted that in the year to date 1,033 new cases of HIV were registered.

That was five times as many as in the whole of 1995 and more than in the whole 10-year period since the Soviet Union's first recorded case. Pokrovsky said the biggest factor in the growth was infections of drug users.

Urging parliament to take steps immediately, Pokrovsky said: "If the programme is not accepted in the near future and is not put into action urgently, then we really will have half a million HIV sufferers in two years time."
On Tuesday, Mikhail Narkevich, a coordinator of Russia's AIDS control programme, also said the country faced an epidemic as HIV infection, especially among drug addicts, rose sharply.

Carriers of the human immuno-deficiency virus (HIV) number some 2,081 while 245 people have the full-blown disease. Some 60 people are estimated to become infected with the HIV-virus every day, Narkevich said.

The figures are still low by international standards -- Russia's population totals 150 million -- but medical experts say they could grow fast because there has been a sharp increase in sexually-transmitted diseases.
Last year, the number of syphilis cases in Russia doubled.
Narkevich said he was alarmed by the trend among drug addicts, where registered HIV carriers now number 750 against just three at the start of this year.

The Russian parliament has passed a law demanding strict measures to stop foreigners bringing AIDS (Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome) into Russia, including a requirement for long-term visitors to prove they do not have HIV.
However the law has not been implemented.
The spread of AIDS in Russia was slowed by the country's relative isolation, conventional sexual behaviour and low drug abuse levels before the 1991 collapse of the Soviet Union.
